:::{#exm-limit}
#### The limit of $3x + 1$ at $2$

$\lim_{x \to 2} (3x + 1) = 7$.
Given $\epsilon > 0$, take $\delta = \epsilon / 3$.
For every $x$ with $0 < \abs{x - 2} < \delta$,
using the [distributive law](algebra.qmd#def-distributive) in the second line,

$$
\ba
\abs{(3x + 1) - 7}
&= \abs{3x - 6}
&& \text{(subtract)}
\\
&= \abs{3(x - 2)}
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\\
&= 3 \abs{x - 2}
&& \text{(} \abs{3y} = 3 \abs{y} \text{, since } 3 > 0 \text{)}
\\
&< 3 \cd \frac{\epsilon}{3}
&& \text{(} \abs{x - 2} < \delta = \epsilon / 3 \text{)}
\\
&= \epsilon
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

For example, with $\epsilon = 0.3$ and $\delta = 0.1$,
the point $x = 2.05$ satisfies $0 < \abs{2.05 - 2} < 0.1$,
and $\abs{(3 \cd 2.05 + 1) - 7} = \abs{7.15 - 7} = 0.15 < 0.3$.

:::
